A root finding algorithm based on knot insertion.
It has linear convergence speed and linear complexity per step.
It requires index operations and memory usage grows with every iteration step, limiting the maximum number of iterations.
For degree 9 (tri-cubic), it has an execution time of 1.0 (relative), MSE 0.034, and max error 0.85.
A root finding method using Regula Falsi combined with De Casteljau subdivision for root isolation.
The method is based on the idea of subdividing the control polygon using the de Casteljau algorithm at the intersection of the control polygon with the zero axis.
It is referenced as [LR81] in the literature.
